groups.description: Compile every local component warning-clean.

Focused Hspec examples for the root package's console: startup and exit integration, and the lua subcommand (LUA-19) run as a child process of the built executable, linked with the bundled Lua interpreter. The command line as direct examples of a pure function (every refusal, every default, every number at its boundary), the status mapping and the signal coordinator's rule (the first signal only requests the stop, the second forces exactly once, overlapping deliveries on many threads force at most once), and every exit status by running the executable: 0 for the checked-in one-shot, looped-with-controller and event-only watcher examples and for runs ended by --ticks and --for, 1 for a failing init, a later failure, a syntax error, a missing file and a failure followed by a signal, 2 for a representative of each class of usage error (including a refusal the runner returns and the top-level unknown argument), and 130 for SIGINT and SIGTERM with the instance's shutdown output on stdout before the process exits; which stream carries print, a table, a warning, a failure report and a usage line. A signal is delivered only after the child has said on stdout that its script is running, every read and every wait is bounded, no example sleeps, and every child is killed and reaped on every way out independently of the signal under test.

Focused Hspec examples for the foundation package's Logging, Resources, Failures, Recovery, Workers, Messaging, and Time contracts. The Resources examples include both scoped collections: the thread-owned collection, and the collection owned by a capability that can be lent to code on other threads, with the same guarantees, the capability checks, serialization of the threads that present it and the scope's exit racing an operation already inside.

Focused Hspec examples for the runtime package's application runner and lifecycle, logging lifetime, reporting, supervision, inbox services, package boundaries, resource smoke, and supervised messaging waits.

Headless Hspec examples for the GLFW package's session, window, command, control, host, dynamic window, monitor, input, and mode models over the test seam, its link declarations against the native manifest, and its package boundaries. Initializes no GLFW and needs no display.
Run the console executable's smoke mode end to end. The executable links the lua packages' bundled interpreter, so this also builds its C sources and the runner through the executable.

Focused Hspec examples for the Lua host package's fault and cancellation transport across the foreign-call boundary, stack and registry discipline, terminal close, independent execution under the threaded RTS, selectable standard libraries (the coroutine library included), the value boundary, and tasks: module entry points run as coroutines on their VM owner, with yield and wait operations, typed refusals wherever a yield cannot reach a scheduler, closing and teardown of suspended coroutines, the scope an owner runs around each of its VM's callbacks, the asynchronous-request binding kind and its wait delivered only to an owner configured with a request context (and refused as not yet supported elsewhere), the protocol model's holders (an owner of requests that is not a task, ended through the revocation a retiring task's requests go through), and its export boundary. It also carries the module loader's examples (LFE-9, selected with --match "the module loader", "the loader's", "stopping the loader" and "failures of the engine"), which run real import chains on real interpreters through the public owner with an injected source supplier, address resolver and eligibility, and never a sleep: depth-first evaluation read from what the modules marked, one table shared by every importer, a separate cache for each VM, a later root never overtaking the current one and a root not started before the coordinator made it eligible, a pending dependency that is also a later root evaluated once within the chain with one interest in its source, every sticky failure kept across a later import, a dependency failure condemning its importer even when the script caught the error, a binding's refusal of a module's call failing the module without ending the owner, completed dependencies surviving a failed parent, cycles reported with their chain and no extra frame, one example for each place Lua can and cannot suspend (a coroutine the script created, a table.sort comparator, a string.gsub callback, a finalizer, a to-be-closed handler, pcall, xpcall and a metamethod), the resolver's refusals latching nothing, a root chosen from the module an import belongs to, the immediate lookup of a hook, the phase of a module's top level with the service a helper or a stashed facade may use only from a hook, the identity, source and chain-depth bounds at and one past each with pending and failed identities charged and a dependency that does not fit failing its importer, a chain stopped at each depth with the pending identities stopped rather than failed, late and duplicate sources refused, failing closes and releases kept beside the first failure, an admission whose supplier raised taken back, a supplier, a resolver and a release that raise, an allocator budget swept over a chain with every outcome classified and the ledger balanced, a source delivered by another thread while every other thread is refused, hooks and stop served while a chain waits, an independent VM unaffected, a seam's re-entry refused, and an external client composing injected sources and the loader through the public owner alone. Deliberate nontermination is a separate local-only probe.

Focused Hspec examples for the Lua runtime adapter's trusted VM owners under real supervision: readiness through a supervised wait that the startup acknowledgement cannot satisfy, owner identity that is never reissued, finite submission and both its bounds, exactly-once settlement with faults of a call returned as data, host failures ending only their own owner under its policy, protected stop and exit records, independent owners, the refused reply wait from inside any Lua callback, and the adapter's dependency closure. Every execution and lifecycle example acquires real VMs. The same suite carries the scheduling machinery's examples for Lua tasks, which need no VM and no sleep: per-owner policy and its refused choices, service classes and quanta, application-granted logical time, elapsed waits and the owned timer under an injected clock and fake wakes, service budgets and attributed overruns, safe-boundary pause, resume and stop with their results, the scheduler's stop, and the aggregate diagnostics. It also carries the scheduled owners' examples, which run real Lua tasks as coroutines on real supervised scheduled owners under the same injected clock and fake wakes: the scheduler's behavior end to end, creation and identity, settlement and its bounds, idle and stop with closing errors retained, host failures and cancellation, refused waits and tick completion, determinism of logical-time work, and the collection a scheduled owner lends to its VM's synchronous callbacks for exactly each callback's duration: members acquired, borrowed and retired during a callback and in a later one, a loan refused after its callback, from a thread it started and from another VM's callback, the loan found by initialization, closing handlers and finalizer-eligible bindings, and retirement releasing what remains on the owner's thread after the VM closed, however the owner ends. It also carries the script instances' examples (LUA-18), which run real instances on the same owners and the same injected clock and fake wakes: each instance's own state beside the module it shares, the hooks, events held while an instance initializes or is paused, a full queue and every refusal, failure and the application's escalation, pause, resume and stop with their results, what each way of ending revokes and counts, every bound, determinism of logical-time work under different delays and budgets, and two sweeps of the configurations that could break the layer's invariants: the order of effects when the scheduler's result places or its admission queue are exhausted, room is freed by each site that frees it and the service budget cuts turns in different places, and the count of a one-shot's owed run whichever way the scheduler took it or refused it, whether a pause took it back, and however the instance ends. It also carries the instance update cadence's examples (LUA-24), on the same owners, injected clock and fake wakes, never a sleep: an interval's exact conversion and its refusals, the first update one interval after init and the duration granted since the previous one finished (less what was granted while paused, handed to Lua as a float number of seconds), cadence points that pass while any invocation is active adding nothing (a callback that waits across a due tick included), a due update's place in the instance's one queue behind earlier events and ahead of later ones and its tick released when it cannot start, pause and stop settlement of a due update, elapsed refreshes coalesced after a stall with no catch-up burst and an elapsed duration rebased at a resume, the owner's one timer shared between instances and an ordinary waiter, the checked arithmetic of accrued durations, ticks and deadlines, and the determinism of logical-time work under different delays and budgets. It also carries the lifecycle services' examples (LUA-23), which run real instances on two or more real supervised scheduled owners, under the same injected clocks and fake wakes with gates and barriers and never a sleep: one registration shared by owners with different grants (an inspection-only grant cannot control, a control-only grant cannot inspect, and an owner with no grant keeps the not-yet-supported fault with its action never run), the refusal of an owner outside the grant, a foreign runtime's identity and an identity never issued alike without a test of the target, stale identities unknown only within the grant, routing by identity and never by label, the refusal of a grant that does not make sense before anything starts, pause, resume and stop across owners with their receipts and results (read once, abandoned, never another instance's), every refusal (a bound held at the caller or at the target, an owner not taking requests, an identity not live), exactly-once settlement whatever ends the target first (a stop, an initialization that fails, an instance that is stopping, the owner's cancellation or retirement), requests never undone and reservations always returned when the caller's instance or owner ends or a task finishes, an instance's control of itself applied only after its segment, bounded coherent inspection of instances and owners, and logical admission by an assigned tick and sequence: controls applied at that tick's boundary before its other work in that order whatever order they arrived in, late, duplicate and unassigned requests refused explicitly, the assignment told only what the engine knows, requests racing the tick that begins theirs, and requests overtaken by the instance's end or the owner's exit. It also carries the instance leases' examples (LUA-22), which run real instances on owners that lend their collection and hold leases, with fake resources and a fake provider and no Lua cleanup code in any module: acquisition from init, callbacks and shutdown through the lent capability; handles that are lost, overwritten or never stored; a constructor that fails part way, rolled back with nothing registered and no handle given; the per-instance capacity and the engine's refusal of an acquisition over it, which a script's pcall does not turn into a host failure; instance versus application leases, a shared asset surviving one instance's exit, and a cached handle staying retired; early and repeated release, the retired handle accepted only by the release operation, and a failing release whose failure is the answer and never runs the cleanup again; the drain on every way an instance ends, newest first and past a failing release, with the failure kept beside the primary one and fatal under every policy; and a provider's retirement that completes later, which holds the stop completion, the capacity and the owner's life through a stop and a cancellation until the provider says it is done. It also carries the asynchronous requests' examples (LUA-7), which run real instances and tasks on real supervised scheduled owners with a fake request provider the examples drive by hand, an injected clock and gates, never a sleep: admission and every refusal as a fault of the call with the provider asked nothing, a place reserved before the provider is asked and held until the settlement is taken and the provider has proved its work over, settlement exactly once on every path (the provider's result or failure, the script's cancel, an instance's stop, failure or failed init, a task's end, an epoch change, the owner's stop, failure and cancellation) with duplicate, late, unknown, oversized and malformed replies counted and never overwriting a settlement, interests admitted in init and in an update and taken in a later invocation, an instance's stop completion and the owner's exit waiting for the provider while what the work needed stays undisposed of, waits that resume at a safe boundary, a settlement retained without resuming a paused instance and a wait in a hook that cannot suspend, a provider that raises, a failing retirement fatal under every policy and failures arising together kept first-primary with the rest as evidence, a completion that never waits for the owner, the finalizer refusals unchanged, settlement at the assigned tick on a logical owner (an early reply held and no settlement, the tick held until the provider completes or the request is cancelled, a cancel before the tick that wins whichever of the reply and the cancel came first and leaves identical effects, late, unassigned and duplicate places, holds shared by requests, cadence work and tick-assigned controls, the order of the places, and determinism across arrival orders), and epochs. It also carries the owned subscriptions' examples (LUA-26), which run real instances on real supervised scheduled owners with a fake event provider the examples drive by hand, an injected clock and gates, never a sleep, and a holder-owned subscription pin in the protocol model's own examples: producers on other threads that never block and never call Lua while the owner is held, ordered events kept in order and refused and counted when the instance's queue has no place, replaceable state coalesced in place keeping its place in the queue and taking none, at capacity, in the delivery the owner already selected, and not once a callback has begun, unsubscribe and stop settling once in either order, a delivery to a subscription that ended refused and counted, every way an instance ends revoking its subscriptions with the provider told once and the stop completing only when the provider proves its retirement, a subscription made in init surviving every callback after it, deliveries retained in order while paused, a refused subscribe as a fault of the call, a delivery failure surfaced to the application's policy, logical admission by an assigned tick and place (reversed and permuted arrivals, late, duplicate and unassigned places, a full store, overflow and coalescing decided at the boundary in the order of the places, queued and individually served grants giving the same admissions, and the tick not waiting on what cannot start), epochs and generations (an old producer unable to reach a new subscription, churn unable to reclaim a place while retirement is pending), a provider that raises, a failing retirement fatal under every policy and failures arising together kept first-primary with the rest as evidence, unfit and throwing deliveries, and every grant that is refused. It also carries the stale-reading examples (#488), which hold the engine inside a transaction while a provider's retirement reading is first polled, commit once from another thread to what the reading and an earlier read of the transaction both read (the request service's state, a TVar two requests' readings share, a TVar two lease retirements' readings share), and require that the reading, counted on every execution including rolled-back attempts, runs at most twenty times from that commit until the engine reports the work over; they use gates and barriers, never a sleep. It also carries the accounting wait's examples (LUA-31, the `Accounting` component, selected with --match "the accounting wait"), on real supervised scheduled owners under the same injected clock and fake wakes, with gates and threads parked in STM and never a sleep: the wait for a scheduled owner's accounting of its accepted grants returning for a tick that did no work, for an owner never granted one and for an owner that hosts no instances, and not returning before a coroutine's closing handler the owner runs at a boundary after the grants finished (a stopped instance's, and a refused wait's), a `shutdown`, a retirement a fake provider completes later with the owner idle, and the application's escalation and its return, each window on its own with tick completion already returned where the window lies after it; the captured grants' final boundary, where a grant accepted after the snapshot overflows a logical wait, fails an instance in that boundary and parks it on a retirement, and the wait holds for the retirement and the callback; prefix isolation (a later, unfinished grant not waited for) and a snapshot kept across a supervised outcome handled while the wait is pending; every scheduler bound exhausted and more waits one after another than any bound allows, with the owner's counters unchanged; cancellation, parked and inside supervision's handling of an outcome; the owner stopped, cancelled, failing recognizably or fatally (an escalating answer and a raising callback included) with an ending owed, and a wait asked of an owner that had ended; the refusal from a Lua callback; and the determinism of logical-time work with no wait, with waits during and after the ticks and with a cancelled wait. It also carries the script runner's examples (LUA-27, the `Runner` component, selected with --match Runner), which run real Lua on real supervised scheduled owners the runner starts, under the same injected clock and fake wakes, with gates and STM signals and never a sleep: every way a source can fail to load (a syntax error, an error at the top level, a missing, unreadable or over-bound file) reported with no TID in script order, a path named twice and two files with one name, a module's identity; the instance's kind from the entries its module defines and every usage refusal with no hook run and the VM retired, the read-only query of which hooks a module defines (defined, absent, present but not a function, running no code, never changing); a failed init, a failing run, update, callback and shutdown each reported once with its stage, several failures in one run in ascending TID order and before the end table, a primary failure kept over a failing shutdown, and failures of the host from a binding and from a sink (while a script prints, while a module loads, and as a table or a report is written) propagating unchanged after the retirement with the first primary and the rest as evidence, a failure another supervised worker latched propagating only after the runner's owner is retired, and cancellations during startup and during cleanup after a failure, none of which ends the wait for the owner (each holds the owner at a gate inside Lua and requires the sink's late line before the call returned); every ending (a one-shot completing, a script stopping itself and another, the stop request, the run limit on the fake timer with an early and a stale wake, a stop request set before the run) with every remaining instance, a paused one included, stopped once in ascending TID order and the timer cancelled on every exit, endings that apply together decided in their order of precedence, and a segment let return; print and warn reaching the output sink and the error sink only, from a module's top level, init, run, a callback and shutdown, and no C stream, with long lines, invalid UTF-8, embedded NUL bytes, line breaks and control characters bounded as written, after escaping, and safe, the standard libraries a script lacks and the originals it cannot reach; the start table taken once every instance has initialized (a gated initializer, a stop before an instance began, an instance that failed early kept) and the end table taken after the VM is retired, both bounded and to the output sink only, the load and failure reports to the error sink only, no table for a run with no instance, and the status value for each combination of failure, stop request and success. It also carries the runner's logical-tick and event examples (LUA-28, the same `Runner` component), on the same injected clock, fake timer, gates and STM signals and never a sleep: every usage refusal of the tick clock (a zero tick duration, an elapsed interval on a tick VM, a tick interval on an elapsed VM, a tick limit without a tick duration, a zero, negative or over-64-bit tick count as limit or as interval) refused before any admission or hook; the driver granting ticks of exactly the tick duration, back-to-back ticks with none skipped, merged or shortened when the clock jumps past several deadlines while a segment is held, nothing for an early or a stale wake, no tick once a stop begins, a deadline the clock cannot represent, and no timer registration left armed on any exit; the tick limit ending the run after exactly its ticks and combining with the duration limit, a tick-limited run with a failed instance or a failed shutdown a failure, every ending of a tick VM (tick limit, duration limit, stop request, a limit arriving mid-tick) stopping each remaining event-only, looped and paused instance once in ascending TID order, scripts stopping and pausing one another ending the run only by every instance having ended, endings that hold together at a tick's boundary decided by the documented order with the runner held in the write of a report, a source that does not load and a failure of the host arriving during a tick; Lua controls placed by the runner in the order they were issued, each in a place of its own, none refused; the instance events (a watcher told of every start and end with a TID it can use with the lifecycle namespace, the name and outcome, a failed init producing only an end, no replay to a later subscriber, one delivery for each subscription in subscription order each with a place of its own, events on arrival on an elapsed VM, and a script with no binding that starts a request); the pure classification of every engine answer to a delivery and the production of events against feeds that answer each way, counting every attempt and raising each defect as a failure of the host; both overload cases with real VMs (a delivery refused when offered because the queue or the staging store is full, counted, and a delivery staged for a tick that finds the queue full at it, failing the watcher once); sequential admission with an init held on both clocks, with a stop request or the duration limit arriving during it; and a scenario with a ready, yielding one-shot, a one-shot that unsubscribes at once and a paused one-shot resumed by a logical control, whose transcript is identical across runs whose pacing differs (the runner held in a report's write or the start table's, the clock far past every deadline, every tick granted late). It also carries the module loader's hosted examples (LFE-9, selected with --match "module loader on a scheduled owner"), on real supervised scheduled owners under the same injected clock and fake wakes, with gates and STM signals and never a sleep: a chain waiting for a source while the owner serves a hook, resumed on the owner when another thread's source arrives; an independent owner not waiting for it; a due logical chain holding the next tick until it ends, with the grant applied afterwards, and a chain a UI asked for holding nothing; the inbox bounded by admitted work (a full inbox, a duplicate notification and a logical root out of order refused); the owner's exit closing the inbox, stopping the waiting chain on the owner and giving its interests back; and a plan refused before anything starts.

Focused Hspec examples for the two-domain Lua sample (LUA-29, D-44): a UI VM owner and a gameplay VM owner composed side by side from the Lua package's public modules, with real interpreters under a real supervision boundary, the UI owner's clock and timer injected where an example moves it by hand, and gates and bounded waits everywhere else. The package and import boundary read from the Cabal description and the imports (no runner, no internal module, nothing of GLFW, Vulkan or the console, no engine package depending on it); both owners' exit records and nothing left live; exposure per owner, no shared global and no handle into the other VM; a staged batch invisible until the commit, exactly one snapshot per completed tick, none for a held tick and none for a tick whose work did not finish; the intention contract (true only once the queue has taken an intention for the next unstarted tick, full at once, a malformed or over-bound call answered as data before the typed binding, never waiting for gameplay); admissions raced against the driver's grants, each settled at the tick it was accepted for; conservation of accepted intentions, applied or rejected as stale exactly once, including a finite session's final grant racing admissions; a coherent view for each UI segment; the UI completing a set number of updates while gameplay is held by a barrier, and while gameplay runs a pure-Lua CPU-bound computation with no hook, counted from the computation's start to its end on the threaded runtime with the tenfold margin; the application-owned seeded random stream; and the sample's executable run as a child process for its report, --help and exit status 2 for an unknown argument and for a malformed value. Then the sample's failure, overload and stop paths (LUA-30): a script failure on the gameplay owner fails the session, which publishes one failure snapshot beside the last good world and tick, with every ordering of a failure and the tick's commit forced by gates (a failure in the last or the only segment, two failures, a wait the scheduler refused in the final segment with a held shutdown), none committing before the failure has settled; the intentions' ledger on every path (applied, stale, invalidated by a failure, discarded by a stop) balancing, with overload answered and counted by cause and the UI never blocking; events a provider delivers, a refused event counted and a delivery failure failing the session; the stop paths, a stop racing a tick, a cancellation of the enclosing scope and one bounded cleanup record for every ending; the gameplay workspace's leases released on every path an instance ends by, a failing release ending the owner fatally and not a recoverable failure; the UI's isolated failure; and the UI's pause and resume as lifecycle controls assigned to ticks, serialized with the tick, with every request counted. Then the sample's deterministic qualification (LUA-8): the canonical encoding of the authoritative state and its SHA-256 digest, pinned to two hand-built golden values, with each covered field changing the digest and each excluded field not changing it; the digest trace of the initial state and of every committed tick, which a tick that did not commit never adds to, and the final digest of the final published snapshot, which a failure or a stop after the last commit changes without touching the trace; the tick-assigned input log, its text format, its writer (one record for each successful admission in tick and place order however the admissions are raced, nothing for an offer that was only made, never a log that has lost a record) and every refusal of its parser, each naming its line; a replay through the admission seam, released tick by tick before each tick begins, with every log that cannot be replayed refused before the session starts, the UI's offers declined and its requests for controls refused before they take a place, and a record the seam would not take raised as a defect; D-23 qualified on the sample, the digest trace identical tick by tick across repeated runs of one input log while segments are held and released at differing points by gates, do differing amounts of spin work, the UI does many more updates, reads, draws and offers than the log holds, the driver's grants are back to back and with gaps, the UI owner runs on the real clock and a log a UI-driven run recorded is replayed with no UI activity at all, three negative controls (a different seed, a record moved to another tick, two intentions on one entity exchanged in place order) that each diverge at the first tick they should, and the failure and pause scenarios reproducing their traces across replays; and the executable's record, replay, digest and expect-digest options with their exit statuses 0, 1 and 2, a recording never overwriting a file and an output error never claiming a recording, and a matching expected digest never overriding a failure's exit status. The executable also runs its failure scenario (exit status 1 with the evidence) and its normal one (exit status 0). The executable is reached through the suite's build-tool dependency and is never launched by a smoke group. No example sleeps.

Local-only optional Linux confinement and resource-limit feasibility probe (LUA-14). Launches confined children through the candidate namespace, private-root, and seccomp profile; records the machine, the permissions, and whether the profile installed at all; and checks the fail-closed refusal, the denied native and Lua accesses with the mechanism that denied each, two-instance isolation and independent termination, the whole-process memory ceiling, the execution bound's escalation, and the three lifetime cases. Built and run on Linux only; on other platforms the components are not built. A green run is evidence, never a supported-platform verdict.

Portable Hspec contracts for the GPU retention and frame-ownership model: typed identities and the misuse they are rejected as, the hold ledger and disposal eligibility, frame ownership phases and their obligations, validated admission budgets and their backpressure, recovery and allocation-retry accounting, and bounded round-robin owner progress under a scripted clock. It runs through the CPU project and needs no Vulkan SDK.

Portable Hspec contracts for the Vulkan diagnostic capture: the production C capture storage driven through its package-local producer entry — bounded copying under one shared text budget and an object limit, error latching ahead of admission, saturation with its drop counter, truncation and capture-failure counting, contained producer failures, and concurrent producers — and the diagnostic lifetime around it: delivery through the caller's logger by a worker in a group of its own, the verdict, sink failure beside a preserved primary failure, and teardown ordering on every exit. It runs through the CPU project and needs no Vulkan SDK.

Portable Hspec and QuickCheck contracts for the math package: vector arithmetic and checked normalization, 4×4 matrix identities, element access and the column-vector multiplication order, translation, scaling and checked axis-angle rotation, the right-handed look-at view, and the perspective projection under every combination of its depth range and clip-space Y direction, with every degenerate or non-finite input returning Nothing. It runs through the CPU project; the library depends on base alone.

Portable Hspec contracts for the Lua-first engine's pure configuration boundary (LFE-3): the strict format-1 launch manifest parsed from supplied bytes, and the fixed M1 profile of limits. The manifest examples with both role orders, the common and per-role entry fallbacks, every one-role variant and the absent vms, with the selected and every declared entry and the exact bytes kept; the byte limit at 65,536 and one past it and the nesting limit at eight containers and nine, each told apart from the schema refusal a well-formed document would get; refused byte order marks, malformed UTF-8, unpaired surrogate escapes, comments, trailing commas and data, non-object roots, control characters, invalid escapes, numbers and literals; duplicate keys after escape decoding at every object, decided before any map is built; the exact numeric reading of format, which accepts every token whose decimal value is exactly 1 and refuses the rest without binary floating point or size-derived work; the identifier grammar, every schema refusal, and a refusal that does not depend on member order; tick_seconds as exact decimal nanoseconds with both endpoints, every forbidden form and overflow; every fixed profile value against an independently written expectation in its unit, the derived values, valid smaller injected profiles and profiles refused as not positive, above the fixed value, overflowing or inconsistent; the manifest and entry boot checkpoint (LFE-6) composed with the content inventory over real temporary folders: the content configuration derived from the fixed profile (10,000 entries, 32 segments, 1,024 and 255 path bytes, 64 MiB per file, 1 GiB per root, a 64 KiB buffer) and from a validated smaller one; a manifest of exactly 65,536 bytes accepted and one of 65,537 refused before it is read, a missing manifest, a root holding only a case-mismatched name and a manifest in the parent folder all refused with no other spelling or folder searched, a directory at the manifest's name refused; the manifest parsed only from the bytes the scan pinned, so a revision replaced between scan and checkpoint, a parse of revision A beside a scan that pinned a valid or equivalent revision B, and a reader returning other bytes are all refused while the same bytes pass; every declared entry, a fully overridden common entry included, validated as a literal reference and required to name an inventoried regular file (invalid text, a missing file, a case mismatch and a directory refused), with each role's own entry chosen and both one-role arrangements preserved; a checkpoint cancelled while it holds the manifest read leaving no borrow and no partial result, and a failing reader propagating as a failure; a separately compiled client composing the root, the scan and the checkpoint through public modules; the M1 behavior selection (LFE-8) with the export-module ceilings the fixed profile gives a VM, 1 MiB of source, 256 identities and a chain of 32 (and the same ceilings of a smaller validated profile), and the Lua host's module loader configured from them (LFE-9): a real in-process owner runs a chain of exactly 32 modules, fails the importer whose dependency would make it 33 and admits nothing for it, and holds 256 identities pending and refuses the 257th; and the package and import boundary. The raw-data provider (LFE-10) is checked through real Lua instances on real supervised owners over a real temporary content root, inventory and read pool: the exact bytes of empty, NUL, non-UTF-8, BOM and line-ending files, taken once and usable after the request retires, repeated reads that repeat the I/O, a file at the 8 MiB ceiling inside the 16 MiB crossing and one byte over as too_large, not_found, content_changed (same-size edit, growth, removal, replacement by a directory, edits after a job was queued), io_error (a real mode 000 file where the process cannot read it, otherwise pending, and an injected one) and a reader defect that fails the owner; the per-VM byte bank at its limit with busy that does no file work and leaks nothing, missing and oversized requests accepted while the bank is full, VMs asking at once for the pool's last slot, and checked bank arithmetic; at most two reads at once with the oldest queued read next, a finished result held for a future tick while its worker runs another read and its bytes stay charged, default and explicit due positions, a late read holding its tick, reversed completion order not changing delivery order, and settlement on arrival; queued and in-progress cancels, an early held result against a cancel, an instance stopping while its read runs, one instance or VM ending while another carries on, an owner stopped repeatedly, every place held while completions still land, and a pool that is down when a request is handed over. It runs through the CPU project, starts no window or GPU, the checkpoint reads only through the verified read it is given, and the one place it starts Lua is the loader example's in-process owner.

Headless Hspec contracts for the content package's anchored native roots, over temporary trees each example owns. A launch path that is relative, absolute or reached through symbolic links opens one directory whose identity and descriptor the root keeps, so renaming it, replacing its old path or retargeting the selection link never switches an open root, while a root opened afterwards selects the new target; every component below the root, the final file included, is opened without following a symbolic link and its type checked on the opened object, with internal links to the same root, to outside targets and dangling ones refused, a component or the final file swapped for a link at a controlled open boundary refused without the outside sentinel ever being read (a check-then-open control reads it under the same swap), a FIFO refused without waiting for a writer and a socket classified as a forbidden type whichever errno the native open reports, plus device kinds, permission denial and missing entries through the adapter seam; strict bounded reads and metadata from the opened object across short reads, read errors, early stop and a pathname replaced mid-read; enumeration with each entry's own kind, lossless non-UTF-8 names (a real one where the filesystem accepts it, a supplied one elsewhere), both names of a hard link as separate paths, entries that changed since they were observed, a depth bound, a directory that reports another device still traversed, and a directory repeating on its active ancestor chain refused with its chain while a repeat on another branch is allowed (identity injected, since no mount is created); and the lifecycle: a root closes only after every borrowing operation has retired and refuses new ones once its exit begins, a cancellation of the exiting thread neither shortens that wait nor is lost, cancellation at each boundary and with a cancellation pending as an open returns closes every descriptor exactly once through the stream when it owns the descriptor, a failed close is retained beside the primary failure and the remaining closes still run, two roots and two concurrent borrowers do not disturb one another, and repeated success, refusal and cancellation return to the starting descriptor count by exact acquisition and close accounting at the adapter seam. Its logical identity policy is checked on pure values and supplied entries: the literal root-relative reference grammar, with every refusal (empty, leading, trailing and repeated slashes, dot and dot-dot segments, backslash, colon, NUL and C0/C1 control characters at their boundaries, and every ill-formed UTF-8 form, none decoded with replacement), literal spaces and non-ASCII names, composed and decomposed spellings sharing one NFC identity while case stays significant, and the byte and segment-count bounds at and one beyond each edge for the raw and the NFC form, shrinking and expanding; a checked mapping from logical names to the exact observed native components that refuses sibling collisions by normalization or canonical caseless comparison (file, directory and mixed, including ancestors no entry supplied), duplicate or structurally inconsistent entries and bad inventory names, stops at its entry allowance and never publishes a partial map, with lookup that is exact and never falls back to a case-insensitive or native spelling; the Unicode tables pinned to 17.0.0 and checked against NormalizationTest and CaseFolding reference files of that version and hand-derived canonical caseless vectors; a real temporary tree enumerated by the content service (hard-linked names stay separate; names the file system cannot hold are reported pending beside the supplied-entry evidence); and a separately compiled client of the public identity interface. Its bounded whole-folder inventory (LFE-6) is checked over real trees and explicit fault and mutation gates: every directory and file scanned including hidden, empty and unused ones, with exact lengths and independently known SHA-256 vectors (a million-byte file read in buffer-sized requests with a one-byte growth probe), unused malformed content inventoried and unused unreadable (injected, and by permission bits where they apply), invalid-named, linked, FIFO or oversized entries refusing the scan with no partial inventory and no retry; the entry allowance (the real 10,000 including the root), path depth (the real 32), path and segment bytes on the supplied and the NFC form, per-file and per-root bytes with hard-link aliases charged per name, each exactly at its edge and one past, short reads, and an enormous directory refused at the entry that crosses the allowance; growth, truncation, an early end of file, a size that disagrees after the read, an entry or directory swapped for a directory or a link between its listing and its opening (the outside sentinel never read), and a directory swapped after it was opened; hard-link aliases and an edit through an outside name, a mounted subtree and active-ancestor cycles (identity injected), the root renamed or its selection link retargeted, and independent roots; a verified read returning exactly the bytes whose length and digest the inventory holds, deciding absent, case-mismatched, directory and too-large keys from the inventory before any open, refusing a same-length edit, a changed length, growth past the ceiling, a missing, retyped or relinked file, and an I/O error, each with no bytes delivered to a recording consumer, accepting a timestamp-only change and identical replacement, never admitting a new path, and delivering only the verified buffer when the file is replaced or edited after it was opened; and descriptor accounting, cancellation at each scan and read gate, the root's exit waiting for a scan or a read, a failed close kept beside the primary refusal and never reported as changed content. Its verified-read worker pool (LFE-10) is checked over real trees and explicit gates: each file's exact bytes (empty, NUL, non-UTF-8, BOM and line endings) returned whole through real verified reads, the allowance at, one past and absent decided before any read, every request repeating its read; at most the configured number of reads at once with the oldest queued job next and the dependency class ahead of unrelated work; the slot reservations that bound the queue, a job or a release beyond them refused as a defect and a consumer releasing its slot inside its own sink; a queued cancel that opens no file, an in-flight cancel, and cancels between issuance and the read and between the read and publication, held at the pool's coordination hooks; the scope closing with queued jobs told they were abandoned and a started read finishing and delivering; a reader defect and a failing sink latching the pool, withdrawing and telling every queued job and rethrown by the scope; a partial startup drained; cancellation during a drain, including a read that cannot be interrupted; the root closing only after a started read; and a separately compiled client composing a root, a scan and a pool from public modules while the pool's hooks and specification constructor stay hidden. A separately compiled client proves the public API hides the name constructor, raw descriptors, reader constructors, the inventory, digest and limit constructors and the private adapter library. It runs through the CPU project and needs no display.

Portable Hspec contracts for the asset-image package's PNG decoder over committed fixture files whose texels the suite states by hand: every colour type at every bit depth, 16-bit components rounded to nearest, palette tRNS alpha, Adam7 interlacing, greyscale and RGB tRNS colour keys honoured at every bit depth by comparing stored samples before any reduction (malformed keys ignored), and colour-space chunks that change no texel; colour images premultiplied in linear light within one code value of an independent reference for every (channel, alpha) pair, exact at alpha 0 and 255, and data images byte-for-byte unchanged; the format, extent and single-level layout the GPU upload endpoint takes; the binary-alpha cutout mark; and the refusal, naming the asset, of empty, foreign, truncated, corrupt-stream and undecodable bytes, each result fully evaluated; and the opt-in bounded static-PNG preflight, through its public entry and an external client: validated limits (zero, negative and above-2^31-1 values refused, no sentinel for unlimited), recognition by bytes with unsupported-format, malformed and exceeded-limit classes in a documented check order, framing and every chunk's CRC, animation markers before or after the image data, every limit at its edge and one past (with the approved M1 maxima), packed-row and empty Adam7 pass scanline counts counted pixel by pixel, IDAT chunk-boundary independence, metadata that is never decompressed, inflation that stops at its budget inside an output piece and across IDAT chunks before a deliberately corrupt continuation is read, results that are fully evaluated and retain only slices of the caller's bytes, and faults and asynchronous exceptions that are never turned into refusals; and the bounded decode of a preflighted PNG (LFE-15), through its public entry and an external client: every fixture whose texels the suite states by hand (every colour type and depth, palette and colour-key transparency compared at the stored depth, 16-bit rounding, 16-bit Adam7 with alpha and keys, Adam7 over narrow and odd extents with empty passes, every filter type at every pixel size, one-byte and empty IDAT chunks, compressed ancillary chunks that are not zlib streams and a metadata decompression bomb that is never expanded) decoded to one premultiplied sRGB RGBA8 level that equals the general decoder's colour image byte for byte, a pixel-exact 16-bit Adam7 noise image whose allocation is checked against what was charged, refusals by class with every charge released, a second pass that meets different bytes and is held to its own inflation bound and checks, and the account contract: each buffer charged before it is allocated, in order, equal to an independent count, the allocation maxima of every colour type, depth and interlace method at the approved dimensions, real decodes at those dimensions, banks too small for each stage, injected bank and release faults retained beside the primary failure, asynchronous cancellation while waiting and after every grant leaving the bank as it was, the output staying charged through the hand-over beside a consumer's staging copy, and repeated success and refusal returning the bank to its start. It runs through the CPU project and needs no GPU.

Portable Hspec contracts for the render-api package's texture handle: construction and access through the backend-facing module at every Word32 edge, in every pairing of index and generation, and over generated values; equality, ordering (by index, then generation) and show; and, through separately compiled external clients that expose only base and the package, that the public module supplies the handle's instances but neither its constructor nor a field reader nor the backend's construction function, while the backend-facing module builds and reads a handle. It runs through the CPU project; the library depends on base alone.

Portable Hspec contracts for the render-2d package's frame value and instance encoding: snapshot validation refusing, with every reason found and its pass, view, layer and instance index, a non-finite or out-of-range UI scale, brightness, fixed half-height, camera, viewport, clear colour, transform and UV rectangle, a depth key of 2^24 or more, a second or non-final window pass and a non-zero clip index, each at its boundary and retained together across locations, including inside a zero-size viewport; offscreen-only snapshots accepted and validated snapshots unchanged; the discrete-step-zoom list's refusals; the 64-byte little-endian instance layout checked field by field against hand-written bytes and an independent reference encoder, for zero, one and many generated instances; the flags word's packing for every sampler choice and flag combination with its reserved bits zero and the clip index in the top 16 bits; the draw plan routing every combination of the cutout conditions (depth-enabled world layer, mark by complete handle, opaque tint, translucent and additive flags), ordering cutouts by submission and the ordered path by ascending depth key and then submission, the equal-key outcomes, layers without depth and UI layers drawing wholly in the ordered path, run partitioning and zero-size viewports, over fixtures and generated snapshots; and, through external clients, that validated values and offscreen target references cannot be forged. It runs through the CPU project and needs no GPU.

Portable Hspec contracts for the render-2d-oracle package's expected pixels, computed from a validated snapshot without a GPU: the camera's position at the viewport's centre, whole-number zoom spacing in both zoom modes, a quarter-turn rotation, UI at content scale 1 and 2 and with a viewport origin, pixel snap moving a sprite rigidly by its origin's rounding including the camera's translation, reflected, singular and unrepresentable quads and unrepresentable mappings, empty and letterboxed viewports; nearest and linear filtering across a texel boundary with clamp-to-edge, sRGB decoding on sampling and encoding on an sRGB target against a UNORM target, 2:1 minified fixtures reading level 1 with each filter and the last level, a probe rotated by 45 degrees or between levels reported indeterminate, the placeholder for an absent handle and for a handle whose generation differs, and BC7 textures sampled through their software-decoded levels; tint, brightness (including a clamped result), additive output and the exactness rule per channel, premultiplied overlap in drawing order, equal keys in submission order, a UI instance with a larger key over one submitted later, view and layer order, nonzero clears, and the 8-bit store after every draw (eight sources of byte 4 give 32); every indeterminate case and every refusal (missing, invalid or disagreeing target metadata, pass and pixel indices, malformed images, incorrectly sized readbacks) at its boundary; the readback reader swizzling B8G8R8A8; and, against hand-written synthetic readbacks, that the oracle rejects reversed overlap, a channel off by two and a wrong snap and accepts the exact image. It runs through the CPU project and needs no GPU.

Vulkan-linked headless Hspec contracts, executed rather than only built, through cabal.project.vulkan against the provisioned native prefix: the native backend's profile and roots decisions over a stand-in native layer (native-tests), its shader contract against the provisioned compiler (shader-tests), the window integration's controller over the GLFW package's scripted seam (integration-tests), the triangle sample's pipeline cache over stand-in builders (triangle-tests), the sprites sample's scene, probe oracle, fixtures and PNG writer (sprites-tests), the scene3d sample's scene, cameras built with the math package, independent probe oracle and PNG writer (scene3d-tests), and the 2D renderer's Vulkan recorder over a stand-in native layer (render-2d-vulkan-tests): the scissor rule against viewportContains, the push-constant packing, the attribute descriptions against the 64-byte instance layout, the sampler-choice mapping, the pure frame work of targets, metrics, mappings and scissors, and the recorded command order, the drawing-order instance bytes at their ring offsets, mixed samplers in one draw, empty scissors recording no draw, pipelines per format, and the refusals of an unknown target, invalid or disagreeing metrics, an unmappable view and a full ring, none of which records a clear or a draw. The Vulkan native suite: the package-native fixture's shared roots under the graphics owner, with GLFW's session on the process main thread, and the migrated VK-2, VK-5, VK-6 and VK-7 cases, VK-17's required profile over the triangle sample's drawing, the sprites sample's window-free evidence case (GRS-8), which writes its PNG and probe record into the group's evidence directory, the scene3d sample's window-free depth-tested evidence case (GRS-10), which writes a PNG a camera pose and its probe record into the same directory, the 2D renderer's ordered-path evidence case (R2D-7), which records eleven render-2d snapshots into offscreen targets through render-2d-vulkan and judges every pixel of every target against the render-2d oracle, writing a PNG a target and a probe record into the same directory, and the synchronization-validation control in private child processes, all with the validation layer and synchronization validation enabled, failing on any validation error or incomplete diagnostic capture after the last teardown. Its executable, and the triangle, sprites and scene3d samples', are built in a separate preparation stage; its native execution — test-owned display, fixtures, examples, retirement, diagnostic finalization and teardown — is measured alone under a 30-second watchdog. On Linux the command starts its own isolated X11 display; on macOS it needs the desktop opt-in on its own command, given under the owner's standing approval for runs an issue or pull request needs.

The Vulkan native suite's whole --complete profile under the isolated headless compositor tools/display/wayland.sh starts inside the timed execution: the shared roots, the migrated VK-2, VK-5, VK-6 and VK-7 cases, VK-17's required profile over the triangle sample's drawing and the synchronization-validation control, every session requesting Wayland by name and the shared session's selected backend asserted before any rendering example, with the validation layer and synchronization validation enabled and failing on any validation error or incomplete diagnostic capture after the last teardown; and WL-4's connection-loss case, a child that ends a compositor of its own while rendering to a Wayland surface. VK-16's hide-and-show case runs and is required there: under Mesa's legacy FIFO on Weston 13 it proves that hiding a presenting window never blocks the graphics owner, and that the shown window presents again on a replacement swapchain. It has test.vulkan-native's preparation stage and inputs, and its native execution — compositor startup and teardown included — is measured alone under a 30-second watchdog. Linux only.

Hspec examples driving the documentation landing helper, this planner and runner, the CI image builder, and the native recipe helper against temporary Git repositories; the quruntul adapter's agreement with this catalog; and the boundary that keeps the Vulkan project out of the mandatory floor, holds its three groups to their commands and routing, and holds the compatibility summary to the retained records it quotes.

Local-only optional headless X11 helper probes using stub servers and window managers, including real 30-second startup deadlines. Never selected automatically or routed to CI; eligible for coordinated local testing. Opens no desktop session.
Real GLFW session, thread, and window examples through the shared native Hspec fixture, on an isolated X11 display.

The native suite's whole Wayland selection, on the isolated headless compositor tools/display/wayland.sh starts: every required case of the Wayland qualification design's D-12 matrix (backend selection, independent window lifetimes, supported controls and observations, explicit unsupported outcomes, wake, shutdown, failure cleanup, and connection loss in children that end compositors of their own), and that both X11 test-check drivers answer unavailable there. Required when affected, with test.glfw-native's inputs; the selector names that tree and nothing else.

LUA-15's local macOS feasibility proof: a confined helper's denied filesystem, network, process, and native-module accesses before and after its mod source loads, two-instance process and storage isolation, the enforced whole-process memory limit and the execution bound, and the three lifetime endings. Optional and Darwin-only; the component is not built elsewhere, so a request for it on Linux fails rather than passing vacuously.
Local-only optional headless Wayland helper probes using stub compositor and client programs, including the real readiness deadline. Opens no desktop session.
Local-only optional nonterminating-Lua cancellation experiment. Deliberately exhausts a five-second observation window in a child process; ordinary Lua contracts remain in lua-host-tests.

Local-only optional probe of the lua subcommand's forced exit (LUA-19, D-42). Runs the built executable with a script whose shutdown never returns, delivers a first SIGINT or SIGTERM after the script reports it is running and a second after it reports its stop has begun, and shows the process exits with status 130 promptly, the hook never having finished. Deliberate nontermination, so never selected by affected inputs; the routine suite covers the rule through the coordinator's examples. Every wait is bounded and the child is killed and reaped independently of the signals under test.

Local-only optional profiling probe of the two-domain Lua sample (LUA-8, D-45, P-11). Runs bounded workloads and prints one record for each, with no threshold and no assertion on a number: the UI's update cadence (the count and the minimum, median, 90th percentile and maximum of the intervals between its completed updates) while gameplay is idle, held inside a running segment and CPU-bound; gameplay's throughput in ticks committed per second of elapsed time with the UI idle and busy; the scheduler's counters for both owners (segments by class, overruns and their sites, queue and active high-water marks, grants); the RTS statistics (collections, major collections, bytes allocated, the collector's pause total, the most live bytes and the live bytes at the end); and a repeat of the qualification runs fifty times each that prints how many matched the baseline's digest trace. It runs under -threaded -with-rtsopts=-N2 -T and prints them. A wall-clock figure is never an input to a check, so it is never selected by affected inputs or by the fallback and needs no CI worker.
